clustering: Phi Algorithm 1 inspired weighted binary Hamming k-means. Exclude all-zero and one-hot input rows. Seed 1701; weighted random distinct-support initialization; maximum 30 iterations; mean exactly 0.5 rounds to zero; empty clusters retain their previous centers. This is an independently specified calibration, not the official Phi artifact or fine-tuning.
assignment: Minimum Hamming distance. Equal distance uses lowest base mask; no base if it cannot strictly reduce the original number of source terms. Zero/one-hot input rows use ordinary bypass.
streaming: Native row order, cache starts cold per tile. One shared LRU wide-value budget for base and residual objects. Only completed resident results match. Fixed base graph compiled offline; on a missing compiled parent construct requested base directly, without recursive replays. Signed residual parent requires same-sign subset. Admit all computed residuals of length at least two. Hold base and residual in two explicit join/compute vector registers outside the shared cache.
variants: precomputed PWP fetch with cache, independent L2
same base graph plus exact residual cache
same base graph plus completed-residual subset cache
counting: Separate vector additions, source-weight reads, signed source negations, wide PWP external requests, shared-cache reads/writes/evictions and original destination commits. No sum reported as time or energy. Phi parallel eight-input reduction and PWP prefetch require a later cycle comparator; these are operation and request counts only.
scope: Calibration/evaluation are disjoint sample IDs from one frozen sequence ledger; not a cross-sequence generalization result. No checkpoint changes, no RTL/PPA, no AEE. All functional checks use exact diagnostic rational theta and signed weights, not frozen floating-point execution.
